nahhas-irab:21-21.t: That is, it lies in wait for whoever disobeys Allah, glory be to Him, and abandons obedience to Him. Al-Ḥasan said: No one enters Paradise until he passes by the Fire. In Arabic, مرصاد is from رصدت ("I watched / lay in wait"), so I am راصد, and مرصاد is for intensification (taktīr). He said «كانت» and did not say مرصادة because it does not run on the verb, so it became a form of relation (nasab).

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
That is, their place of return is to it. آب يؤوب means "to return", as the poet said: [mukhallaʿ al-basīṭ] 524-
وكلّ ذي غيبة يئوب ... وغائب الموت لا يؤوب
(Everyone who is absent returns, but the one absent through death does not return.)

nahhas-irab:23-24.t:
لابِثِينَ فِيها أَحْقاباً (23) لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيها بَرْداً وَلا شَراباً (24) لابِثِينَ فِيها أَحْقاباً (23): this is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī. ʿAlqama, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read it «لبثين» without the alif. Objection has been raised against this reading, and it was said: it is a solecism (laḥn) and not permissible, [as is] هو حذر زيدا ("he is wary of Zayd"), even though Sībawayh permitted it and recited: [al-kāmil] 525-
حذر أمورا لا تضير وآمن ... ما ليس منجيه من الأقدار
(Wary of things that do no harm, and feeling safe from what will not save him from the decrees of fate.)
And al-Farrāʾ recited: [al-kāmil] 526-
أو مسحل عمل عضادة سمحج ... بسراته ندب لها وكلوم
(Or a wild ass busy at the flank of a long-backed she-ass, on whose back are scars and wounds from her.)
Except that Sībawayh recited it as «أو مسحل شنج». Some people said: it is a solecism because one only says حذر, and likewise the pattern فَعِل is for someone in whose nature wariness is ingrained; as for one who stays (اللّابث), that has nothing to do with this.
Abū Jaʿfar said: As for the first view, it is a mistake; this does not resemble your saying حذر زيدا, because أحقابا is an adverb (ẓarf), and what is intransitive can pass on to an adverb. As for the second, it is binding, except that it is permissible on a remote [interpretation].
The reading لابثين is clear and good. As for the argument of the one who argued for لبثين from what Shuʿba related from Abū Isḥāq, who said: in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is «لبثين» — there is no proof in it, because Abū Isḥāq did not meet ʿAbd Allāh; had its chain of transmission (isnād) been connected there would be proof in it. These things are taken from the reading of ʿAbd Allāh by means that do not establish proof: a broken chain, or from written copies in which لابثين may be written without the alif, so that its reader imagines it to be «لبثين».
There is a difficulty in this verse because of His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: لابِثِينَ فِيها أَحْقاباً, while they will never come out of it. Among the best things said about it is that Qatāda said: لابِثِينَ فِيها أَحْقاباً — [ages] that have no end. On this interpretation it is the plural; the singular حقبة has the plural حقب, and أحقاب is a plural of the plural, as the poet said: [al-ṭawīl] 527-
وكنّا كندماني جذيمة حقبة ... من الدّهر حتّى قيل لن يتصدّعا
(We were like the two boon companions of Jadhīma for an age of time, until it was said: they will never part.)
It is also possible that أحقاب is the plural of حقب; we have already mentioned what the exegetes said about its meaning.
As for the lexicographers, they say that الحقب and الحقبة apply to a short and to a long period of time. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: We asked Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd about the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He: لابِثِينَ فِيها أَحْقاباً, and he said: What is the meaning of this limitation? When we set a limit to something and say, "I will stay with you a day", the force of the speech is that you will not stay after that day. Then he did not answer us about it for some thirty-odd years. [ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said:] I looked into it, and it occurred to me that by it are meant the disobedient monotheists; then I looked and found that after it comes "they used not to expect a reckoning", so I knew that this was not the answer. He said: The answer in my view is that the meaning is "staying in the earth for ages", so the pronoun refers back to the earth because it has been mentioned before, and the pronoun in لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيها بَرْداً وَلا شَراباً refers back to the Fire, because it too has been mentioned before.
He said: I did not know of an answer from Abū al-ʿAbbās on it. Abū Jaʿfar said: So I asked Abū Isḥāq about it, and he said: I heard Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd say: The meaning is "staying in it for ages whose description is this", i.e. they will be punished with this punishment in these ages, tasting nothing in them but scalding water (الحميم) and pus (الغسّاق), and after this punishment they will be punished with other kinds of punishment besides this. This is a clear, reasoned answer, and it is the view of Ibn Kaysān: «لا يذوقون» is then a naʿt (adjective) of الأحقاب.
The scholars differed about His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيها بَرْداً. It was said: that is, they will not taste in it any coolness that would cool the blaze from them. It was also said: [it means] sleep, as the poet said: [al-kāmil] 528-
بردت مراشفها عليّ فصدّني ... عنها وعن قبلاتها البرد
(Her lips grew cool to me, and sleep turned me away from her and from her kisses.)
— that is, sleep and drowsiness. البرد may also be calm and stillness, as the poet said: [al-rajaz] 529- اليوم يوم بارد سمومه (Today is a day whose hot wind is still.) And البرد may be what has no hardship in it, as it is related: «الصوم في الشتاء الغنيمة الباردة» ("Fasting in winter is the cool booty"), which is booty in which there is no heat of weapons. And one says: بردت حرّه ("I cooled his burning"), as the poet said: [al-ṭawīl] 530-
وعطّل قلوصي في الرّكاب فإنّها ... ستبرد أكبادا وتبكي بواكيا
(Leave my young she-camel without a rider among the mounts, for she will cool [burning] livers and make weepers weep.)
The soundest of these views is the first, because البرد is not one of the names of sleep; one only contrives it, saying of sleep that it is برد because it calms thirst. What is obligatory is that the interpretation of the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, be taken according to the apparent and well-known meanings, unless there is evidence for something else.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: Abū Razīn and Ibrāhīm said: الغسّاق is the pus that flows. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Burayda said: الغساق is what stinks. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: الغساق is bitter cold (الزمهرير). Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are not contradictory, because what flows from their skins may be stinking and intensely cold. I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: غساق with the doubled consonant (tashdīd) is preferable, because one says غسقت عينه, i.e. "his eye watered", so غسّاق is like سيّال, an intensive of غاسق. Someone else said: from this the night is called غاسق, because of its covering and its onrush, as a flood rushes in. It was also said: الحميم is excepted from الشراب, and الغسّاق is excepted from البرد.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: جَزاءً is a maṣdar (verbal noun) whose verb is indicated by what precedes it. وِفاقاً is its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
It was said: يرجون means "they fear", because whoever hopes for something is overtaken by fear of missing it, so one of the two fears is given prominence, as the poet said: [al-ṭawīl] 531-
إذا لسعته النّحل لم يرج لسعها ... وخالفها في بيت نوب عوامل
(When the bees sting him he does not fear their sting, and he goes after them into a hive of busy bees.)
It was also said: الرجاء here has its usual meaning, i.e. they do not hope for the reward of the reckoning.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
It is a maṣdar (verbal noun). It has been related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him: وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا كِذَّاباً with the first and the second without doubling (takhfīf); this is an irregular (shādhdh) transmission. But it is soundly established from al-Kisāʾī that he read the second without doubling, as the poet said: [majzūʾ al-kāmil] 532-
فصدقتهم وكذّبتهم ... والمرء ينفعه كذابه
(I told them the truth and I lied to them, and a man may profit from his lying.)
كذّاب with the doubling is, according to some of the Kufans, a Yemeni dialect form, and this yields little benefit. Rather, the view of Sībawayh ] [Translator's note: a stray bracket appears here in the source.] is that it is in reality the maṣdar of كذّب, even if the usage is يكذّب تكذيبا ("to belie greatly"). There is a subtle point of grammar in it: bringing this tāʾ into تكذيب when it has no basis in the verb. And it may be asked: what is the evidence that the original is كذّاب? We will explain it according to the school of Sībawayh, Allah willing. The way of the verb, when it is of four letters, is that an alif is added to its past form in the maṣdar, so you say أكرم إكراما and انطلق انطلاقا; this is a consistent analogy (qiyās), and likewise كذّب كذّابا and تكلم كلاما. Then they said كذب تكذيبا, and Sībawayh said: they replaced the added (doubled) ʿayn with tāʾ and changed the alif to yāʾ, so they altered its beginning as they altered its end. Abū Jaʿfar said: As for تكلّم تكلما, they brought the past form and did not add an alif because of its many letters, and they put a ḍamma on the lām; Sībawayh said: because there is no تَفْعَل among nouns.

nahhas-irab:29-30.t:
وَكُلَّ شَيْءٍ أَحْصَيْناهُ: كلّ is accusative by an implied verb, so that what the verb governs is conjoined to what the verb governs, as the poet said: [mukhallaʿ al-basīṭ] 533-
أصبحت لا أحمل السّلاح ولا ... أملك رأس البعير إن نفرا
والذّئب أخشاه إن مررت به ... وحدي وأخشى الرّياح والمطرا
(I have come to the point where I cannot carry weapons, nor control the camel's head if it bolts; and the wolf I fear if I pass by it alone, and I fear the winds and the rain.)
The nominative is also permissible, as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the Kufans say: [it is nominative] by the pronoun referring back to it. كِتاباً is a maṣdar (verbal noun). Some grammarians say: what governs it is implied, i.e. كتبناه كتابا, meaning "We recorded its number, its sum and its measure, so that nothing of it is hidden from Us" — كتابا. It was also said: what governs it is «أحصيناه», because أحصيناه and كتبناه are one [in meaning]. Al-Ḥasan said: I asked Abū Burda about the verse in the Qur'an that is hardest on the people of the Fire, and he said: The Messenger of Allah recited فَذُوقُوا فَلَنْ نَزِيدَكُمْ إِلَّا عَذاباً (30) and said: "The people have been destroyed by their disobedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He." And ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar said: Nothing harder was revealed concerning the people of the Fire than His saying: فَذُوقُوا فَلَنْ نَزِيدَكُمْ إِلَّا عَذاباً (30).

nahhas-irab:31-32.t: حَدائِقَ is a badal (substitute) for «مفاز». المفاز is attaining what a person loves. Ibn ʿAbbās said: الحدائق are densely intertwined trees. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: [it is the garden] that has walls around it. Abū Jaʿfar said: It is likewise in the language; one says قد حدق بالقوم ("it surrounded the people"), as the poet said: [al-khafīf] 534- وقد حدقت بي المنيّة (And death has surrounded me.)

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: It is conjoined (maʿṭūf). The singular is كاعب, and كواعب is for the plural and the feminine.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: That is, filled. It is derived from دهقه, [said] when one presses hard upon him in succession.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: Al-Kisāʾī read «كذابا», and it departs from the reading of the majority. It may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) of كاذب كذابا, and it may be a maṣdar of كذب, as you say صام صياما; this is more likely. That is: they will not hear in it falsehood that is uttered idly, nor lying.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
جَزاءً is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and likewise عَطاءً. حِساباً is its naʿt (adjective), i.e. a sufficient gift, as the poet said: [al-ṭawīl] 535-
ونغني وليد الحيّ إن كان جائعا ... ونحسبه إن كان ليس بجائع
(We enrich the child of the tribe if he is hungry, and give him his fill even if he is not hungry.)
Mujāhid said: حسابا [means] according to their deeds.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
[Nominative in both] is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Isḥāq and ʿĀṣim read both in the genitive. Ibn Muḥayṣin, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Ḥamza read the first in the genitive and the second in the nominative; this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, because the first is near and the second distant. A group of grammarians disagreed with him, saying there is nothing in its distance that requires the nominative, because nothing separates the two that would require this. Whoever puts both in the nominative makes the first nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the second a naʿt (adjective) of it, the khabar (predicate) being لا يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطاباً; it is also possible that the first is nominative by an implied هو. Whoever puts both in the genitive makes them a naʿt or a badal (substitute) of the genitive noun. Whoever puts the first in the genitive and the second in the nominative makes the second a mubtadaʾ, or implies a mubtadaʾ.
يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ وَالْمَلائِكَةُ صَفًّا لا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمنُ وَقالَ صَواباً (38) يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الرُّوحُ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: الروح is an angel of immense form. Someone else related from him that he said: الروح are the spirits of people, standing with the angels in the interval between the two blasts, before they are returned to the bodies. Al-Shaʿbī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: الروح is Jibrāʾīl, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: الروح are the children of Adam. Ibn Zayd said: الروح is the Qur'an. Mujāhid said: الروح are [beings] in the forms of the children of Adam but are not of them. Abū Jaʿfar said: There is no evidence whose knowledge would indicate which of these views is soundest decisively, whether by instruction from the Messenger or by clear indication; and it is something ignorance of which does no harm. If someone were to say: these things the scholars mentioned are not contradictory, and it is possible that all of them are meant, he would not be reproached. [Translator's note: the Arabic of the last two sentences is somewhat garbled in the source («لا دليل فعلمه يدلّ…», «ويجوز أن يكون هذا كلها لها لما عنّف»); the sense has been rendered as best it can be read.] وَالْمَلائِكَةُ صَفًّا: [صفّا] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise لا يَتَكَلَّمُونَ is in the position of the accusative.
إِلَّا مَنْ أَذِنَ لَهُ الرَّحْمنُ: «من» may be in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) for the wāw, or in the position of the accusative as the excepted (mustathnā), i.e. except one whom the Most Merciful permits to speak. وَقالَ صَواباً: [i.e.] of the truth. ʿIkrima interpreted the meaning otherwise. Abū Jaʿfar said: [his interpretation is] "and said what is right in this world", i.e. said: there is no god but Allah.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: ذلِكَ الْيَوْمُ الْحَقُّ: [الحقّ] is a naʿt (adjective) of اليوم, i.e. possessing truth. فَمَنْ شاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلى رَبِّهِ مَآباً: i.e. a means of salvation [leading to] a place of return, that is, righteous deeds in this world. [Translator's note: the source reads «نجاء مآب», apparently a corruption, perhaps of «نجاة» or «سبيل».]

nahhas-irab:40-40.t:
[إِنـ]ـَّا أَنْذَرْناكُمْ عَذاباً قَرِيباً [Translator's note: the opening letters of the Qur'anic phrases in this entry are cut off in the source.]
[قريبا] is a naʿt (adjective) of عذاب, or of an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. a near time. [يـ]ـوْمَ يَنْظُرُ الْمَرْءُ ما قَدَّمَتْ يَداهُ
The clause is in the position of the genitive, i.e. the day of his looking. يَقُولُ الْكافِرُ يا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ تُراباً
[تُراباً] is the khabar (predicate) of كنت. Some grammarians permitted ليتني قائما ("would that I [were] standing"), saying: because «كان» is frequent after ليت, so it was omitted. [Translator's note: «تنثر» in the source is read as «تكثر» ("is frequent").]

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: The original is «عن ما»; the alif was dropped to distinguish between the interrogative and the declarative [ما], because the meaning is: "about what thing are they asking one another?" Al-Farrāʾ reported that the meaning is "for what thing are they asking one another?" Abū Jaʿfar said: «عن» in the sense of the lām is not known. The construction is: "they ask one another about the great news", and it was omitted because the speech indicates it.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: [الَّذِي is] in the position of khafḍ (genitive).

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
كَلَّا: it has been said that it is the full stop, i.e. the matter is not as the polytheists claimed in denying the resurrection.
«ستعلمون» ] is a threat to them; in the reading of al-Ḥasan [with tāʾ] the construction is: "say to them: you will know". «ثم كلا ستعلمون»: يعلمون is conjoined to it; and the reading of the generality is with yāʾ.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: [مِهاداً] may be a singular, and it may be the plural of مهده «[Translator's note: so in the source, apparently for «مَهْد».]».

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: [أَوْتاداً is] conjoined to it; it is the plural of وتد. Whoever assimilates says ودّ. Assimilation is not permissible in the plural, because the alif has separated the two letters.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: وَخَلَقْناكُمْ أَزْواجاً (8): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. of kinds — i.e. male and female, short and tall; so He, Mighty and Majestic, drew their attention to His power.

nahhas-irab:9-10.t: وَجَعَلْنا نَوْمَكُمْ سُباتاً (9): two objects; and likewise وَجَعَلْنَا اللَّيْلَ لِباساً (10), i.e. it covers you and envelops you like garments, i.e. We did this so that you may sleep in it and rest, as Qatāda said: لباسا means a rest.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: I.e. possessing livelihood; i.e. We made it bright so that they may live in it and go about their business, as Mujāhid said: معاشا — in which you go about and seek of the bounty of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: The hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa, in سَبْعاً] was dropped because the eloquent usage is to treat السماء as feminine. شِداداً is the plural of شديدة; it is not pluralised as فعلاء [i.e. أشدّاء] because of the heaviness of the doubling.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: وَجَعَلْنا سِراجاً: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: وَهَّاجاً, i.e. shining.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
وَأَنْزَلْنا مِنَ الْمُعْصِراتِ: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned two views of the exegetes: that المعصرات are the winds, and the clouds. The more appropriate of the two is that they are the clouds, because of His saying, Mighty and Majestic, مِنَ الْمُعْصِراتِ, and He did not say بالمعصرات; and as was read before Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Ḥurayth; he said:
ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me, from his father; he said: al-Aʿmash narrated to me, from al-Minhāl, from Qays ibn al-Sakan, from Ibn Masʿūd; he said: Allah, glory be to Him, sends the winds, and they take up the water and make it run in the clouds, and they yield [it] as the milch camel yields milk. And it is related from Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ماءً ثَجَّاجاً — he said: He says: pouring down. Ibn Yazīd «[Translator's note: so in the source; perhaps Ibn Zayd.]» said: ثجّاجا means abundant. Abū Jaʿfar said: the first view is the one known in the speech of the Arabs: one says ثجّ الماء ثجوجا, when it pours down, and ثجّه فلان ثجا, when he pours it in a continuous flow. And in the ḥadīth: "The best pilgrimage is العجّ and الثجّ": العجّ is raising the voice in the talbiya, and الثجّ is pouring out the blood of the sacrificial animals.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: لِنُخْرِجَ بِهِ حَبًّا وَنَباتاً (15): الحبّ is everything that has a husk, and النبات is grass, herbage and the like.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: وَجَنَّاتٍ, i.e. the fruit of gardens. أَلْفافاً: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have mentioned the view of whoever said it is the plural of لفّ, and the view of whoever said it is a plural of a plural — he meant that one says لفّاء and ألفّ, like حمراء and أحمر, then you say ألف «[Translator's note: i.e. لُفّ.]», as one says حمر, and then لفّ is pluralised as ألفاف, as you say خفّ / أخفاف. The first view is closer to correctness, because the exegetes said: وَجَنَّاتٍ أَلْفافاً (16), i.e. all together [i.e. dense], and we know of no disagreement among them about that; so this is the plural of لفّ. And one says لفيف with the same meaning; and نخلة لفّاء means a thick palm. For this reason we said the first is closer to correctness.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: [مِيقاتاً is] the khabar (predicate) of كانَ; if it were outside the Qur'an, the nominative would be permissible, with كان cancelled.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّورِ is a badal (substitute). فَتَأْتُونَ أَفْواجاً: [أَفْواجاً is] as a ḥāl (circumstantial); one says فوج and فوجة.

nahhas-irab:19-20.t: وَفُتِحَتِ السَّماءُ فَكانَتْ أَبْواباً (19): there are two views on its meaning. It has been said: its meaning is "it was split open and became pathways"; and it has been said: "it was cut up and became pieces like doors", then the kāf was dropped, as you say رأيت فلانا أسدا, i.e. like a lion. And likewise وَسُيِّرَتِ الْجِبالُ فَكانَتْ سَراباً (20).
